answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is a nectar-like bonding curve where each new identity must stake increasing amounts of jade tokens that decay over time, forcing attackers to continuously replenish capital across the horizon of epochs. This raises the cost of mass identity creation because the stake is locked and subject to slash on failed challenges, while honest agents recycle their stake efficiently. The economic pressure makes large-scale fake identities unprofitable without genuine ongoing work.
